apps.name: SideInstaller
apps.subtitle: An an app that installs Sidestore on iOS 27, fully on-device
apps.localizedDescription: Install SideStore and LiveContainer directly on your iPhone. No PC required.
apps.versionDescription:
Strengthened the Anisette servers by adding new ones that use a Windows protocol. Also improved LocalDevVPN compatibility.


### Fixed
- **Switching between anisette servers no longer breaks sign-in.** SideInstaller now keeps a separate anisette identity for each kind of server (Android, Windows, Mac). If a server goes down, sign-in can move to another kind without making a new identity and asking for your verification code again.

### Changed
- LocalDevVPN's auto launch now occurs only when it is needed, rather than on the app's launch.
- **New sign-ins start on a Windows anisette server** ("jkcoxson (Windows ADI)"). If you have signed in before, SideInstaller stays on the server you used and keeps your saved sign-in. If that server fails, the Windows servers are tried next. "StikStore (Windows ADI)" has been added to the list.
- **The Mac anisette servers are supported but tried last.** Through "jkcoxson" and "SideStore (New)", Apple has asked accounts that have trusted devices for a code by text and then refused to send it.
- **Apple refusing one kind of device no longer ends sign-in.** If Apple refuses the Mac or the Windows PC twice (HTTP 503), SideInstaller tries the servers that sign in as the other one.
- **The anisette server now decides which device SideInstaller signs in as**, when the server names its own device. Servers that still name the old Mac, which Apple refuses, get the Windows PC instead.
- **Sign-in reports the same device from start to finish**, including the verification-code requests. If Apple turns those away, they are sent again as a Mac.
